title: Sectionwise flat module presheaves give finite-limit-preserving tensor functors
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$, and let $P$ be a presheaf of $R$-modules [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Assume that $P(V)$ is a flat $R(V)$-module for every object $V$: tensoring with $P(V)$ preserves injective maps of $R(V)$-modules. Define $T_P$ on presheaves of $R$-modules by $T_P(A)=A\otimes_{p,R}P$ and $T_P(f)=f\otimes1$, using the presheaf tensor product [def-pur-presheaf-tensor-product]. Then $T_P$ preserves finite limits. More explicitly, for every presheaf-module morphism $f:A\to B$, the canonical morphism $(\ker f)\otimes_{p,R}P\to\ker(f\otimes1)$ is an isomorphism compatible with the kernel inclusions. For every finite family $(A_i)_{i\in I}$, the canonical morphism $(\prod_i A_i)\otimes_{p,R}P\to\prod_i(A_i\otimes_{p,R}P)$ induced by the projections is an isomorphism, including $I=\varnothing$. Both comparisons are morphisms of presheaves with the given semilinear restriction maps.

source.place: Tag 03ES (lemma-flatness-presheaves), with the finite-limit formulation of presheaf flatness in Tag 03ER (definition-flat), (1); explicit kernel and finite-product comparisons extracted from the sectionwise proof.

proof.text: At each object V, the hypothesis hP V supplies Module.Flat for P(V). Mathlib.RingTheory.Flat.CategoryTheory packages the exactness of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] as finite-limit preservation of tensorRight (P.obj V). Given a limiting cone of any finite diagram of module presheaves, apply evaluation at V, which preserves finite limits, and then this flat tensor functor. The resulting cone is definitionally the evaluation of the cone mapped by tensorRight P, since [def-pur-presheaf-tensor-product] and its action on morphisms are sectionwise.

Apply PresheafOfModules.evaluationJointlyReflectsLimits to the mapped cone and the sectionwise limiting cones from step 1. This proves that tensorRight P preserves the limit of every finite diagram, including the empty diagram. The joint reflection construction builds module-presheaf morphisms and their naturality, so no separate restriction-map argument is necessary.

Install the finite-limit preservation from step 2. For each f use Limits.PreservesKernel.iso; its forward map is kernelComparison f (tensorRight P), whose composite with the target kernel inclusion is the tensor of the original inclusion. For any finite index type I in any universe, finite-limit preservation implies preservation of its discrete product diagram, and hence IsIso (piComparison (tensorRight P) A). These are the canonical categorical comparisons, so their components are natural and linear. Finite-products preservation handles the empty family as well.
